Definition: apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame:--smoke.
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible, týphō means to smoke, to smoulder. In Matthew 12:20, smoking flax shall he not quench. In the Greek text the word is spelled τύφομαι.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the smoking flax of Matthew 12 is me on my weakest day, and Christ will not quench it.
